- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1239-1249 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: PR-named review runs are accepted without verifying that `head_branch` is the default branch, allowing a forged run to suppress retriggers or consume the changes-lost retry budget.
  WHY: A workflow dispatched from a non-default branch can use a matching title and path to be counted as a peer run, blocking legitimate recovery.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:294-317, 320-327 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_active_run_count` accepts PR-named runs without verifying that `head_branch` is the default branch, unlike the hand-off verification path.
  WHY: A forged active run can keep the checker waiting and block hand-off to the Claude fixer even though its review result would not be accepted.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:17663-17664 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: When a short page causes the helper to stop before querying the second wrapper, its incomplete-listing diagnostic omits whether that wrapper had matching runs.
  WHY: An operator investigating a stalled PR cannot tell from the log whether the consumer wrapper was reached; callers already skip dispatch or push on incomplete results.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:~1700-1720 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The Bug B SHA verification error message treats every return code other than 0 or 1 as “has no codex-agent checkout,” although return code 3 means there is no `codex-agent` job.
  WHY: The message conflates distinct failure modes and makes log triage harder; the retry path has the same message pattern.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:294-317 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A failed repo-wide `actions/runs` listing now raises `ReadError` rather than treating a per-workflow 404 as zero, causing affected open PRs to receive `action: retry` during transient API failures.
  WHY: This documented fail-closed behavior can cause a wider cascade of retry verdicts, including in consumer repos that never had `internal-review.yml`; the reviewer notes the fail direction is correct.
